notable.name: German
notable.note: co-official in South Tyrol/Alto Adige; bilingual road signage near the Austrian border

terrainDescription.zh: 北部有阿爾卑斯山與波河平原農業帶，中南部及沿海為典型地中海型氣候與丘陵地形，境內多山（亞平寧山脈縱貫全國）。
terrainDescription.en: The Alps and the agricultural Po Valley dominate the north; the center, south, and coastline have a classic Mediterranean climate and hilly terrain, with the Apennines running the length of the country.

plate.color: white background, black text, front & rear identical

roadInfra.bollardStyle: Distinctive vertical red rectangle set inside a black diagonal stripe on the front face (black extends to the top of the bollard); the rear face shows a white rectangle instead of red — a rare "vertical rectangle" design shared only with Albania

utilityPole.transformerMount: Round concrete poles are unusually common for a Mediterranean country, often with a distinctive concrete "trident" pole-top; the less-common wooden poles typically carry a small white sticker

historicalContext.zh: 全國以標準義大利語為主，但南提洛爾（上阿迪傑）因鄰近奧地利而以德語共同官方語言呈現雙語路牌，西北部奧斯塔谷則與法語共同官方，是義大利境內少見的多語言邊境地帶。
historicalContext.en: Standard Italian dominates nationally, but South Tyrol (Alto Adige) near the Austrian border has German as a co-official language with bilingual signage, and the northwestern Aosta Valley is co-official with French — genuine multilingual border pockets within an otherwise monolingual country.
